Barnfloor
bärn´flōr
n. (the threshing-floor; the place of a harvest that has failed)
From barn (Old English bere-aern, barley-house) + floor. The KJV uses the compound once, at 2 Kings 6:27, where the prophet's answer names the two places a starving city would normally find food — the threshing-floor and the winepress — and both are empty.

Biblical Definition

Samaria is under siege and a starving woman appeals to the king, who answers with a question that is half despair and half confession: “And he said, If the LORD do not help thee, whence shall I help thee? out of the barnfloor, or out of the winepress?” (2 Kings 6:27). The two places named are the ordinary sources — grain from the threshing-floor, wine from the press — and in a besieged city both are bare. The king is right that nothing but the LORD can help, and it is worth noting what he does next: he swears to kill Elisha for it. A true statement about God is not the same as faith in God. Scripture treats the threshing-floor as the appointed place of harvest and of meeting: “And now is not Boaz of our kindred, with whose maidens thou wast? Behold, he winnoweth barley to night in the threshingfloor” (Ruth 3:2), where Ruth's redemption is settled. Hosea uses the same floor for judgment: “Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud, and as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney” (Hosea 13:3). And Joel shows the siege from the invader's side: “They shall run to and fro in the city; they shall run upon the wall, they shall climb up upon the houses; they shall enter in at the windows like a thief” (Joel 2:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a barn as a covered building for securing grain, hay and flax; and a barn-floor as the floor of a barn — in Scripture, the threshing-floor.

expand to see more

BARN, n. [Sax. bern, from bere, barley, and ern, a place.] A covered building for securing grain, hay, flax, and other productions of the earth.

BARN-FLOOR, n. The floor of a barn; the threshing-floor.

THRESHING-FLOOR, n. A floor or area, on which grain is beaten out.

WINEPRESS, n. A place where grapes are pressed, and the juice expressed.

FAMINE, n. [L. fames, hunger.] Scarcity of food; dearth; a general want of provisions sufficient for the inhabitants of a country or besieged place.

Key Scripture

2 Kings 6:27 — "And he said, If the LORD do not help thee, whence shall I help thee? out of the barnfloor, or out of the winepress?"

Ruth 3:2 — "And now is not Boaz of our kindred, with whose maidens thou wast? Behold, he winnoweth barley to night in the threshingfloor."

Hosea 13:3 — "Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud, and as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney."

Joel 2:9 — "They shall run to and fro in the city; they shall run upon the wall, they shall climb up upon the houses; they shall enter in at the windows like a thief."

Modern Corruption

A right statement about God's sole sufficiency is mistaken for faith, when the king who made it turned in the same hour to kill the prophet.

expand to see more

The king's sentence in 2 Kings 6:27 is theologically flawless. If the LORD does not help, no barnfloor and no winepress will. It is the sort of line that would be quoted approvingly in a sermon. Two verses later he vows that Elisha's head shall not stand on him this day, because he has concluded that the famine is the prophet's doing. Orthodoxy on the lips and rage at God's messenger in the heart can coexist in one man in one conversation, and Scripture puts them side by side so no one can plead the confession as evidence of the faith.

The barnfloor itself is worth holding onto. In Ruth it is where a redeemer is found; in Hosea it is where the chaff is separated; at Araunah's floor it becomes the site of the temple. A threshing-floor is the place where what is real is beaten out of what merely surrounded it, which is exactly what a famine does to a man's religion. The king was on that floor and did not know it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew goren (H1637), a threshing-floor; yeqeb (H3342), a winepress; raab (H7458), famine; mots (H4671), chaff.

expand to see more

Hebrew goren (H1637) — a threshing-floor; rendered barnfloor at 2 Kings 6:27.

Hebrew yeqeb (H3342) — a winepress, the trough that receives the juice.

Hebrew raab (H7458) — hunger, famine; the siege condition of Samaria.

Hebrew zarah (H2219) — to winnow, scatter; Ruth 3:2, Boaz winnowing barley.

Hebrew mots (H4671) — chaff; what the floor exists to separate out.

Usage

"“Out of the barnfloor, or out of the winepress?” — the two ordinary sources, both empty."

"“If the LORD do not help thee” — true, and not yet faith."

"“He winnoweth barley to night” — the same floor, where a redeemer was found."
